title: Reduce GPU memory: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, and arena tuning
author: Diego Morales
description: Motivation: multi-tenant GPU clusters were occasionally OOMing during long-context workloads and throughput targets suffered on 40GB instances. This PR reduces peak GPU memory and transient workspace allocations by combining three orthogonal changes: 1) make activation checkpointing adaptive for small/medium sequences and enable a low-overhead heuristic to checkpoint only transformer blocks with large intermediate activations; 2) implement a scratch buffer re-use scheme that reduces ephemeral allocations for fused kernels and runtime ops; 3) tune the arena allocator thresholds to keep long-lived KV buffers outside of short-lived arenas and reduce fragmentation. Changes include runtime knobs to enable/disable each optimization, a conservative default profile that prioritizes safety, and an opt-in aggressive profile for Dedicated customers. Results: synthetic and internal BERT/LLama-like benchmarks show median peak memory reduction of 24%-40% depending on model and sequence length, 6%-12% throughput improvement in high-concurrency scenarios due to fewer OOM/GC spikes, and stable latency p50/p95 within SLA. Also added stress tests and perf profiles. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime config; staged rollout starting with Dedicated canaries, then host-wide opt-in; telemetry and regression alerts added to Console. Backwards compatibility: no model format changes; flags default to off for older release branches. See linked Linear items for evaluation artifacts and perf dashboards.

review_comments: Ava Chen: Could you add a fallback path when the checkpointing heuristic misclassifies small blocks? We had a regression in ENG-6122 when heuristics were too aggressive.
Diego Morales: Added a conservative path and an opt-in aggressive profile. The tests include an intentionally misclassified block to validate fallback.
Marcus Rivera: The scratch buffer pool looks good but please ensure we don't starve memory for other subsystems; suggest exposing a hard cap metric.
Diego Morales: Exposed pool_high_water_mark and added telemetry to Console; also added unit tests verifying respect of hard cap.
Priya Nair: CI failed on Windows GPU build initially; was the Docker base image change intentional?
Diego Morales: That was my mistake, updated the Dockerfile.gpu to pin CUDA toolkit to the supported patch version; CI now passes.
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU memory via adaptive activation checkpointing, scratch buffer reuse, and arena allocator tuning. Default safe profile enabled; aggressive profile available for Dedicated customers. Improves memory headroom and reduces OOMs under long-context workloads.
notes: Performance numbers in perf dashboards ENG-7204. Aggressive profile should be validated by customers before enabling on constrained instances.
